scope_note: adding it requires a BERMLAUNCH-SCOPE.md revision under §18

problem.fact: claimResidual sends 100% of the residual to ONE immutable address; there is no sub-split
problem.why_time_boxed: residualRecipient is immutable at construction, so the creator's share is capable only of what its destination is capable of, from the first block
problem.without_it: the creator can still pay people later, but only as a revocable off-protocol promise

blast_radius.sits: entirely downstream of the community share
blast_radius.supporter_payment_path: claimBuyback pays directly from the Distributor
blast_radius.worst_case: a defect strands the creator's own money and cannot reach a single supporter
blast_radius.consequence: a different risk category from modifying the claim path

model.kind: per-commitment baseline, not a cumulative range
model.baseline: totalReceived at the moment the commitment is made
model.property: a commitment pays only on value arriving after it exists; retroactive grants are impossible
model.solvency: structural: sum(entitlement_i) + creatorEntitlement == totalReceived by definition; each entitlement floors so the remainder always lands with the creator, never against a payee

immutables.committer: the only address that may commit

maxAllocatedBps.purpose: bounds the damage of a compromised committer key
maxAllocatedBps.at_10000: a stolen key can permanently zero the creator's stream
maxAllocatedBps.at_5000: a stolen key cannot take more than half

sync.why: the Distributor PUSHES weth here, so arrival emits no callback; sync measures balanceOf(this) against totalReceived - sum(withdrawn) and books the delta, same shape as syncExternalDeposit()

commit.power: may only reduce the committer's own future share; can never touch an existing commitment

withdraw.why: destination is immutable and no price is involved — same reasoning that makes harvest() and claimResidual() permissionless
withdraw.consequence: nobody needs gas to be PAID, only to pay

invariants.statement: no function modifies or removes an existing Commitment except its withdrawn field
a commitment pays zero on value received before its baseline
committing does not change any existing commitment's entitlement
committing does not reduce creatorEntitlement at the moment of commit
rounding remainder always accrues to the creator, never against a payee
there is NO function that revokes, reduces, reassigns, pauses or sweeps
invariants.proof_method: enumerate the ABI and assert no such selector exists, in the shape of the existing bindLaunch one-shot proof

must_fail.condition: commit from any address other than committer
native ETH sent to the contract

deliberately_not_failures: two commitments to the same recipient — they simply both pay
a commitment to the committer itself
withdraw when claimable is zero — returns 0 rather than reverting, so a batch relayer is not griefed by one empty payee
sync() when the delta is zero

test_vectors.method: generated from a reference model and machine-checked for solvency at every step
test_vectors.requirement: reproduce exactly; a step that does not sum to totalReceived is a failed run, not a rounding note

critical_steps.V4: commit A at 1500 bps AFTER 1e18 already arrived and was withdrawn -> A entitlement is 0. No retroactive grant, no insolvency.
critical_steps.V6: commit B at 500 bps -> A's entitlement is byte-identically unchanged (I-4)

steps.step: V2 1e18 arrives, no commitments -> all creator
V4 commit A 1500bps AFTER 1e18 already arrived
V6 commit B 500bps; A entitlement MUST be unchanged
V9 dust amount of 7 wei arrives

deployment_ordering.why: residualRecipient is a Distributor constructor argument and immutable
sequence: deploy BermResidualSplitter with creatorRecipient, committer, maxAllocatedBps
deploy the Distributor with residualRecipient = <splitter address>
deployment_ordering.cost_if_never_used: with allocatedBps == 0 the splitter is a pass-through and the creator receives 100%, identical to deploying with a plain address

create2_variant.what: compute the address in advance from keccak(initCode) and name it before deployment
create2_variant.makes_it_verifiable_if: the init code and salt are published — then it is a cryptographic commitment, not a trust assumption
create2_variant.limit: it defers the deploy transaction, NOT the design; the init code must be final to publish its hash
create2_variant.must_not_ship: naming a CREATE2 address without publishing the init code — for that window nobody can verify what governs the money

out_of_scope.item: revoking, reducing or reassigning a commitment

out_of_scope.reason: a mutable splitter is a promise
structurally impossible; this contract only ever sees residual
baseline is the only time dimension
COHORT_COUNT is 3 and hardcoded; GRADUATION and FOMO already provide post-launch cohorts from the COMMUNITY share. This contract is only for slices of the creator's own share.

disclosure_owed_if_it_ships.sovereignty_md: committer is a named authority: it may permanently reduce the creator's own future share up to maxAllocatedBps and nothing else — it cannot revoke, cannot reach committed value, and cannot touch any supporter pocket
disclosure_owed_if_it_ships.public_page: distinguish a COMMITTED slice (as permanent as a Founding pocket) from the UNCOMMITTED remainder (the creator's, carrying no promise at all)
